name: GS23659- Ubuzima Clean Water Project
description:
The Ubuzima Clean Water Project targets peri-urban and rural communities in Rwanda, where many households and institutions still rely on collecting unsafe water and purifying it by boiling over wood-fueled stoves. This practice generates greenhouse gas emissions and exposes families to harmful indoor air pollution. Providing safe drinking water without the need for fuel will directly reduce emissions while improving health and livelihoods across participating communities.

Many existing water sources in Rwanda are either inadequate or in disrepair due to limited maintenance capacity and insufficient water treatment. Under this Voluntary Programme of Activity, Water For People, in collaboration with government authorities and local operators, will install, rehabilitate, and maintain water points to deliver reliable, safe water to communities.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
poa_project_name: Water for People – Clean Water Access Programme in Africa

The PoA "Water for People – Clean Water Access Programme in Africa" targets peri-urban and rural communities and institutions in Rwanda, Malawi, and Uganda, where many still rely on unsafe water sources and purify their water by boiling it over wood-fueled stoves. name: GS23645-VPA-1 Wells of Life: Sustainable Safe Water for Malawi
description: The Wells of Life – Sustainable Safe Water for Malawi is a voluntary carbon mitigation Programme of Activities (PoA) registered under the Gold Standard for the Global Goals (GS4GG), coordinated and managed by EOS Climate and Energy Ltd as the Coordinating and Managing Entity (CME). The Programme is designed to improve continuous access to safe and reliable drinking water in underserved communities in Malawi, while reducing greenhouse gas emissions associated with the boiling of drinking water using non-renewable biomass fuels. VPA-1, the first real case Voluntary Project Activity under the PoA, covers 19 solar-powered groundwater well systems implemented across the Southern Region of Malawi, spanning the districts of Machinga, Zomba, Mulanje, Thyolo, and Blantyre. The Programme applies the Safe Drinking Water Supply (SDWS v2.0) methodology and contributes to SDG 3, 5, 6, 7, 13, and 15. No financial burden is placed on end-users; access to safe drinking water is provided free of charge to beneficiary communities.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
poa_project_name: EOS Climate – High-Integrity Climate & Social Impact Programme

name: EOS Climate – High-Integrity Climate & Social Impact Programme
description:
The EOS Climate – High-Integrity Climate & Social Impact Programme is a Programme of Activities (PoA) developed under the Gold Standard for the Global Goals (GS4GG) framework, aligned with the Paris Agreement. The Programme is coordinated and managed by EOS Climate as the Coordinating and Managing Entity (CME).
The Programme addresses greenhouse gas emissions associated with the use of non-renewable biomass fuels for boiling and sterilizing water in rural and peri-urban communities across Malawi. In the baseline scenario, households rely on unsafe water sources and boil water using firewood or charcoal, resulting in adverse health impacts, time burdens on women and children, local deforestation, and significant GHG emissions.
The Programme enables access to safe, reliable, and continuous drinking water through the installation of solar-powered artesian borehole systems with communal tap stands. All project activities operate with zero direct GHG emissions, eliminating the need for biomass combustion at the point of water use.
The geographical boundary is national in scope, covering eligible rural and peri-urban areas across Malawi. Individual Voluntary Project Activities (VPAs) are developed and included under the PoA framework over time, in accordance with Gold Standard requirements.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: GS23301 GS23422 RVPA-2 Rwanda Safe Water Filter Project by SPOUTS
description:
The purpose of the VPA is to disseminate Household Water Treatment (HWT) technologies in domestic households and Institutional Water Treatment technologies (IWT) in Early Childhood Development Centers (ECD)  in the Republic of Rwanda, Africa. These water purification systems (WPS) are distributed to beneficiaries which were earlier using wood and/or charcoal on rudimentary stoves for boiling water or were consuming untreated water. The project makes the end-users energy efficient and reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions otherwise resulting from the burning of non-renewable woody biomass and/or charcoal for boiling unsafe water to make it safe for consumption. The WPS distributed under this VPA are ceramic water filters and consume no electricity or fuel. 
 
The project boundary is the geographical boundary of Rwanda where these WPS are distributed to households and ECDs in phased implementation throughout the crediting period.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals
poa_project_name: SPOUTS Distributed Technology Devices Program in Rwanda

name: GS12980-GS12981-OYU - Clean Water for Future Leaders
description: The primary purpose of this project is to address the acute water crisis in Tanzania by providing sustainable access to safe drinking water for households, institutional buildings, and nearby communities through water stations. A key aspect of the project is the improvement of public health by reducing the incidence of waterborne diseases such as cholera, dysentery, and typhoid. Additionally, the project emphasizes community engagement and education, involving local communities in the maintenance and management of water systems and educating them on best practices for water use and hygiene. The project alleviates the burden of water collection on women and girls, freeing up time for education and economic activities. It will also reduce energy consumption by minimizing the need for boiling water with wood or charcoal, thereby lowering energy costs and deforestation. Furthermore, the project will promote decent work and economic growth by generating local jobs in the installation, maintenance, and distribution of water purification systems, fostering economic development.

name: GS23168-GS23169-OYU - Clean Water for Malawian Communities
description: The primary objective of this project is to rehabilitate broken and non-functional boreholes to provide clean and safe drinking water to local communities in Malawi. This initiative addresses the need for alternative water purification methods, reducing the reliance on boiling water for drinking purposes and thereby improving the living conditions of the population. The project alleviates the burden on rural women and children, who often bear the responsibility of collecting water and firewood by ensuring access to clean drinking water within 1 kilometre of households. Consequently, this project reduces carbon dioxide emissions associated with the combustion process traditionally used for water purification. In addition to its environmental impact, the project significantly enhances the quality of life, health, and socio-economic status of beneficiaries in the water-stressed regions of Malawi. It includes hygiene awareness campaigns to improve sanitation among local inhabitants. Furthermore, it creates employment opportunities for young people through installing and maintaining rehabilitated boreholes.

name: TerraClear Safe Drinking Water in Laos 💦
description:
In Laos consistent access to safe, potable water remains a critical challenge, forcing many rural communities to rely on contaminated sources. To mitigate health risks, households traditionally boil water over biomass and charcoal fires—a practice that is labor intensive, environmentally taxing, and is a significant contributor to deforestation and indoor air pollution.
TerraClear, a social enterprise based in Laos, addresses this issue through the manufacture and distribution of locally produced ceramic water filters. These gravity-fed household treatment systems require zero energy input, providing a sustainable, emissions-free alternative to traditional boiling. By replacing carbon-intensive water treatment with this clean technology, the project directly reduces greenhouse gas emissions and waterborne diseases while simultaneously improving school attendance and productivity. With the support of carbon finance, TerraClear will continue to scale its operations to reach hundreds of thousands of families and create sustainable jobs in rural areas, ensuring that clean water access no longer comes at the cost of vital forest resources.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: US SecondCrop Microbial Carbon Removal (USSC25)
description: The US SecondCrop Project removes atmospheric CO₂ by applying CarbonBuilder, a patented fungal seed coating, to corn and soybean crops across US Midwest farmland. Root-associated fungi intercept plant-derived carbon and convert it into Mineral-Associated Organic Carbon (MAOC), physically bound to soil minerals and proven to persist for centuries. No land use change, new equipment, or altered crop rotations are required.
gsf_standards_version: Gold Standard for the Global Goals

name: KPC Arakan 1 Project
description:
KPC intends to develop a bamboo plantation designed to address socio-economic and environmental challenges in the Philippines.  Bamboo is known for its high carbon sequestration capabilities.  One of our goals is to contribute to greenhouse gas (GHG) removals thereby generating high integrity carbon credits representing verified greenhouse gas removals over the crediting period and also providing jobs and economic returns to the IP communities.

The geographic region of the project is in Cotabato province in the Philippines within the two Municipalities of President Roxas and Arakan. The project will be implemented on IPs’ ancestral lands within the defined project boundary.

The project will provide a sustainable and steady source of livelihood for IP communities that will help address rural poverty and will provide the new generation of IP’s better opportunities in life. It will foster rural development, strengthen food security, and promote social stability through sustainable employment generation. It will also foster collaboration between the private and public sectors to further develop the Philippine bamboo industry.
